section_path: FY 2025 EXPENDITURE AUTHORITY CROSSWALK - ORIGINAL TO FINAL ESTIMATES 1/

text:
FY 2025 GENERAL FUND ADJUSTMENTS

FY 2025 Budget Revisions — The preceding chart illustrates the changes to the FY 2025 budget from the August 2024 publication of the FY 2025 Appropriations Report (which included changes through the 56th Legislature, Second Regular Session) to the current estimate in this FY 2026 Appropriations Report. The chart includes the changes from the passage of bills in the First Regular Session of the 57th Legislature addressing the FY 2025 budget.

Original Budget Estimate — When the FY 2025 Appropriations Report was published in August 2024, the FY 2025 budget was anticipated to have a \$96 million balance.

Mid-Year Balance — As estimated in the January 2025 JLBC Baseline, higher-than-expected revenues together with other changes led to the state’s projected FY 2025 \$96 million ending balance increasing to a projected balance of \$904 million. The components of this \$808 million increase in the fund balance compared to the August 2024 figures were as follows:

Increased FY 2024 Carry-Forward 324

Increase in Net FY 2025 Ongoing Revenues 389

Fund Transfers Technical Adjustment 2

Decreased FY 2025 Expenditures 93   
Total \$808

The original FY 2025 budget assumed an FY 2024 carryforward balance of \$639 million. Subsequent to the publication of the FY 2025 Appropriations Report, the state's final FY 2024 ending balance was significantly higher than this estimate as final FY 2024 revenues were stronger than anticipated. As a result, the FY 2024 ending balance was \$963 million, or \$324 million above the original estimate.

FY 2025 GENERAL FUND ADJUSTMENTS

The enacted FY 2025 budget assumed ongoing FY 2025 revenues (excluding Urban Revenue Sharing) would increase by 3.0% compared to FY 2024. While the subsequent JLBC Baseline reduced this FY 2025 revenue growth rate slightly to 2.7%, applying this new forecast to the much higher final FY 2024 revenue base ultimately resulted in net FY 2025 ongoing revenues being significantly higher than originally projected, with an FY 2025 ongoing revenue forecast that was \$389 million above the original budget projections.

The enacted FY 2025 budget assumed \$32 million of fund transfers from certain dedicated agency accounts to the General Fund. Based on the technical processing of certain transfers for FY 2024, approximately \$2 million of scheduled transfers were delayed and ultimately shifted into FY 2025.

Finally, the January 2025 JLBC Baseline assumed that spending would be \$(93) million less than the enacted budget. This was primarily the result of offsetting factors: 1) Higher costs in formula programs such as ADE Basic State Aid (including the impact of the Qasimyar property tax litigation) and the state's Developmentally Disabled program in DES; and 2) Lower Medicaid spending due to declining AHCCCS caseloads and savings from the disaster recovery adjustment to the state's federal Medicaid match rate.

2025 Legislative Session — Laws 2025, Chapter 233, the General Appropriations Act, and other budget bills were signed by the Governor on June 27, 2025. The bills made spending changes totaling \$155 million to the FY 2025 budget. The FY 2025 budget changes were as follows:

Shift FMAP Reduction to Revenue Scoring 220

Increased K-12 Formula Supplemental 42

• Net ADC Ex-appropriation (19)

Shift DES DD Supplemental to Other Funds (76)

Administrative Adjustment Estimates (46)

All Other Changes 34   
Total \$155

FY 2025 GENERAL FUND ADJUSTMENTS

In addition, the revised FY 2025 budget assumed \$343 million of increased revenues, which includes: 1) \$145.1 million for revenue performance higher than assumed in the Baseline, based primarily on the April FAC forecast along with a one-time adjustment for revenue gains during the spring tax filing season; 2) A loss of \$(4.4) million for additional revenue adjustments, related to tax law changes and fund transfers; 3) \$131.1 million of additional revenue associated with scoring the savings from the disaster recovery adjustment to the state's federal Medicaid match rate; and 4) \$71.2 million due to the delayed FY 2024 General Fund deposit associated with Valleywise Health instead occurring in FY 2025.

As noted above, the JLBC Baseline projected an FY 2025 ending balance of \$904 million. The \$343 million of additional revenues, combined with the \$155 million post-Baseline net spending increase, results in the FY 2025 budget as passed in June having an estimated FY 2025 ending balance of \$1.09 billion.
